gaps: Phase 1 by design (1-still-port): no motion library wired; the layers carry ARC's motion end-values as inline still-state and swap instantly. Phase 2 replaces the style carrier with @humanspeak/svelte-motion without a structural edit — Portal stays unconditional, forceMount is already on Content + Overlay (mapping §8.2: Portal takes no forceMount).

Unmount policy: ARC unmounts the portal subtree after the exit animation (AnimatePresence); Phase 1 keeps the layers mounted under forceMount with visibility: hidden still-state so a mid-flight toggle can retarget once Phase 2 lands. Settled-DOM delta: hidden nodes remain in the document (out of the a11y tree); pointer-events:none while closed is owned by the verbatim CSS !important.

Consumer callback surface: ARC's onPointerDownOutside → bits-ui's onInteractOutside (mapping §6). Event model differs — Radix fires the callback on the click and hands over the triggering press via event.detail.originalEvent, so ARC compares that original press timestamp against the last open-change; bits-ui hands the raw PointerEvent and fires it at the outside pointerdown itself for mouse/pen (10 ms debounce), deferring to the following click only for touch. The port compares event.timeStamp against the same timestamp mirror — guard intent preserved 1:1: a press that began before the current open-change (e.g. the press that reopened a mid-exit dialog) cannot immediately close it.

Controlled semantics: ARC freezes a controlled dialog when the consumer ignores onOpenChange; the port follows Svelte conventions — use bind:open for two-way, and the internal handler also assigns the bound prop when one exists.
Title DOM: bits-ui renders div[role=heading][aria-level=2]; Radix rendered an h2. Level default matches (2); element differs.
SwapText: Phase 1 renders the swap span's end value only; the rise/blur cross-fade on title/description change is Phase 2.
Bare-root keyframes path retained for DialogContent under a non-ARC Dialog.Root (open === null branch, CSS keyframes keyed off data-state).

bits-ui asymmetry: Dialog.Content's DEFAULT children path mounts ScrollLock unconditionally, so under our required forceMount a CLOSED dialog held body pointer-events:none + overflow:hidden — the whole page was input-dead (caught by the runtime gate, not by any static gate). The port renders through bits-ui's child-snippet path, which gates the lock on open and spreads the identical merged props onto the same div; DOM shape and props are unchanged, and the body lock now engages only while open (Radix parity).
